applies_why: The judge text evaluates the collision between Romans 1:3 descent according to the flesh and the Holy Ghost conception and declares the paternity issue underdetermined for lack of explicit textual resolution, so it is performing the kind of witness-against-link weighing K-C governs.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'without explicit textual resolution of paternity': one reading is that the judge demands an explicit verse resolving paternity (the retired stating-verse test); the other is that the judge merely notes the chain-by-footing balance is unresolved.
why: The judge labels the point underdetermined for lack of explicit textual resolution, which uses the retired stating-verse requirement instead of weighing the competing chains by footing.
